analysis: The supplied units are BASE text of .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml. The head diff is only a truncated patch excerpt, and the changed-range map lists many head ranges that I cannot see. The visible hunk adds a 'Choose this job's Actions cache' step to build-cluster. It sets CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off when the runner name starts with darkbloom- and DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL is unset. It also reworks the runner-routing comments, so the build jobs get the approval's pinned macOS size when job sizes are off instead of falling back to Blacksmith. The base text shows these controls, which this PR does not weaken in the visible portion: permissions are contents: read, persist-credentials is false, actions are pinned by SHA, and SAVE_CACHES is true only for push to master or dev, or dispatch on dev. Pull requests restore caches but do not save them. The strict_cache input keeps release-bound builds from reusing another recipe's objects. The new step only skips cache use and cannot widen cache-write authority in the visible hunk. This is CI-only. It touches none of the provider runtime assets (A-001 to A-020), the wire boundaries (TB-002, TB-011), or the prefix-cache threat T-041 that was supplied as context. No provider key, attestation, authorization, cache-storage, or consumer-data behavior changes. Unverified: the later hunks (the changed head ranges around 107-132, 182-194, 219-257, 312-374, 795-857, 914-976, 1033-1088, 1202-1265) and the ci-plan checks, the provider-ci-build and provider-ci-products actions, and provider-plan.yml were not supplied. Whether every cache step honors CI_ACTIONS_CACHE=off, and whether the new runner routing changes where untrusted PR code runs or which cache a pull request can reach, needs a pass over the full head diff. No concrete regression can be cited from the visible evidence.
